title: Experiment pacing and reserve planning for latency-sensitive features
creator: Marco Reyes
description: Background: Several recent feature rollouts (low-latency assistant, streaming result pipeline) have suffered transient latency spikes for P95 during canary ramps. Current experiment playbooks optimize for quality and error-rate but lack an explicit pacing & reserve budget for latency-sensitive routes. Goal: produce a runbook, traffic pacing policy, and metric contract that lets PMs and SREs safely ramp latency-sensitive features with predictable headroom and cost guardrails. Scope: product-facing canaries and A/B tests for routes marked as 'latency-sensitive' in the catalog. Out of scope: background batch jobs and non-real-time embedding endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Traffic pacing policy defined with clear step sizes, minimal dwell times, and enforced reserve margin for latency-sensitive routes
A2: Runbook published (Confluence) with play-by-play for automated rollback and manual interventions
A3: Dashboard showing expected vs observed latency headroom during simulated ramps
A4: Thresholds for auto-abort/rollback implemented in Canary controller (ENG) and tested in staging
A5: Playbook validated in one cross-functional pilot (assistant streaming) with no customer-facing incidents
evaluation_metrics: Error rate (5xx and token-level failures) during ramp
SLO breach probability for latency-sensitive routes
Cost delta per 100k tokens at each ramp tier
Rate of auto-abort triggers and manual escalations
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Design: finalize step sizes, reserve margin percentage (default 30% headroom), and observability hooks
Phase 1 - Staging validation: simulate traffic patterns with chaos-induced tail latency and confirm dashboard expectations
Phase 2 - Pilot canary (0.5% -> 2% -> 10%): run pilot on assistant streaming for 48h with automated rollback enabled
Phase 3 - Guided ramp: broaden to targeted customers with 1-week dwell at 10% with manual ops on-call
Phase 4 - Rollout: standardize policy into the experiment orchestration UI and include default latency-aware presets
monitoring_playbooks: Primary dashboard: /dashboards/latency-sensitive-experiments - shows headroom, request distribution, queue depth
Alert: Latency headroom < reserve margin for 10m -> P0 runbook initiation
Alert: Error rate spike > 2x baseline for 5m -> auto-abort canary and page on-call
Evaluation hook: sample outputs for correctness drift linked to eval-suite (PM-52013)

notes: Trade-offs: larger reserve reduces ramp speed and increases cost; smaller reserve increases risk of user-facing latency spikes. Default 30% is conservative but can be tuned per product.
Implementation hints for ENG: expose 'reserve_headroom_pct' and 'max_step_pct' on canary resource; integrate with existing auto-abort hooks.
Potential follow-ups: automation to recommend reserve based on historical tail-latency by route, surfaced in Optimize recommendations.
Customer impact: high for enterprise customers running synchronous chat; prioritize pilots on enterprise tenants with SLO contracts.
